core_claim.quote: According to the theory, the A component of this larger representation would not include any of the physical, mechanistic details of the real process of attention, and so it would appear to depict a physically impossible entity, a process that can accomplish the same things as attention without the mechanistic basis for doing so.

source.citation: Graziano MSA, Webb TW. The attention schema theory: a mechanistic account of subjective awareness. Frontiers in Psychology 6:500, 2015

prediction.statement: A system that has a simplified model of its own attention, whose contents reach its thinking and speech, will say it has a non-physical inner awareness of what it attends to; the claim takes that form because the model leaves out the mechanism.

first_stated.passage: This brain would conclude that it possesses a fundamentally mysterious property: a mental possession of something, a subjective awareness.

source.citation: Graziano MSA, Webb TW. The attention schema theory: a mechanistic account of subjective awareness. Frontiers in Psychology 6:500, 2015

prediction.test_for: An artificial agent given a simplified model of its own attention, and a way to describe what that model contains, describes itself as having something that takes hold of items without any physical means; a matched agent without the model does not.
prediction.test_against: Such an agent describes its attention in mechanical terms, or a matched agent with no model of attention makes the same claims of inner awareness for the same reasons.

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: Thus, any cognitive or linguistic access to an attention schema would result in people claiming to have an essentially nonphysical essence inside of them that can shift its state fluidly, take vivid mental possession of items, and empower oneself to decide and to act.

source.citation: Graziano MSA. A conceptual framework for consciousness. PNAS 119(18):e2116933119, 2022

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: Fifth, an attention schema gives technologists a potential lead on constructing artificial consciousness: machines that believe, think, and claim to be conscious according to the same principles that people do, and that receive the same computational and behavioral benefit from it.
